structured_output.summary: Phase 23's package-security chunk delivers genuine, independently verifiable offline qualification. The new clean-package wrapper (scripts/check-management-package.py) packages from a detached worktree whose fingerprint must equal the reviewed source, then binds the receipt to the package script, wrapper, old-consumer manifest, retained archive bytes, the complete archive member ledger, a full src/examples source-inventory equality check, per-file byte equality for every packaged source and legal notice, and explicit per-consumer execution indices. tools/management_consumers.py pins the four published 0.2.2 consumer sources to the verified registry archive c908cad8… and the phase-20 release receipt and requires current bytes to equal published bytes, so old-consumer compatibility is tested against real published sources rather than re-authored stand-ins. The recorded receipt contains all 71 commands at exit 0 against source 7cfc104b…, including both compilers' clean packages (148 no-default-features and 208 all-features lib tests, doctests, example runs, external-crate consumer runs), 14 compiler/feature matrices with fmt+clippy on MSRV 1.89, native export probes over 3820 frozen capabilities, a fresh RustSec audit (0 vulnerabilities, lockfile unchanged), and a source-bound private-material receipt. The offline/live boundary holds: contracts/qualification.json reports liveVerified 0 and liveReceipt null, live_evidence.py and check-access-release.py are deliberately excluded with documented reasons, and tools/management_consumers.py prints executionClaimed false. Gate ordering, CI-subset non-substitutability and documented command counts are all test-enforced. The checkpoint resume feature is source-fingerprint-bound, command-plan-bound, passing-prefix-only, receipt/archive-byte-bound and age-bounded. One real defect: the synthesized external consumer crate declares no features, so the published red_team_dataplane.rs consumer compiles its empty cfg(not(feature="red-team")) fallback, making that newly added external-consumer execution binding vacuous for one of four consumers; the compatibility claim survives only via the in-archive all-features example run. Remaining issues are low: the final receipt never re-verifies checkpoint bindings, receipt verification does not bind the verifying host/compiler identity, one unreachable archive guard, and one test file whose formatting departs sharply from the repository norm. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The synthesized external consumer crate (consumer/Cargo.toml copied from contracts/native-probes/Cargo.toml) declares no [features] table, so cfg(feature = "...") in a consumer main.rs is always false. The published 0.2.2 consumer examples/red_team_dataplane.rs gates its entire body on #[cfg(feature = "red-team")] with an empty #[cfg(not(feature = "red-team"))] fn main() {} fallback, so the external consumer run at check index 13 in docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json and docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.99.0.json compiled and ran only the no-op fallback (confirmed by five 'unexpected cfg condition value: red-team' warnings and empty stdout). scripts/check-management-package.py:105-111 nevertheless accepts that record as an 'External consumer execution binding', and docs/CI.md presents external consumer execution as phase 23 package evidence. One of four newly gated external consumer executions therefore proves only that the file parses as a crate root. The underlying compatibility claim is still supported independently by the in-archive 'cargo run --example red_team_dataplane --all-features' at check index 6, so this is an evidence-integrity overstatement rather than an unsupported acceptance criterion.
findings.required_fix: Add the features the frozen consumers gate on to the generated consumer manifest (for example a '[features]\nred-team = []' section, or forward the scm-sdk feature set) so the cfg-selected consumer body actually compiles and executes, and strengthen scripts/check-management-package.py to reject a vacuous run (for example by requiring the expected stdout marker, or by recording per-consumer cfg selection). If the vacuity is accepted instead, remove the 'external consumer execution' label for that consumer and state the limitation explicitly in the receipt's limitations array and docs/CI.md.

findings.description: The final phase report's 'passed' computation (and tools/review_phase.py:201-218 check_evidence) never re-verifies the per-record checkpoint_bindings against current bytes. read_checkpoint validates them once at resume start, and docs/checks is excluded from the source fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15), so a receipt produced by an earlier command in the same resumed session could be replaced later in that session without invalidating the final report. Only the two package receipts are re-verified, by the final --verify-package-receipts gate.
findings.required_fix: Recompute and compare checkpoint_bindings for every record when writing the final docs/checks/phase-N.json report, and verify them again in review_phase.check_evidence before a receipt can qualify a review.

findings.description: verify_receipt validates schemaVersion, sourceSha256, toolchain, passed, requireClean and effectiveDirty, and requires each recorded cargo command to carry '+<toolchain>' and '--target <report hostTarget>', but it never binds report['hostTarget'] or report['rustcVersion'] to the environment performing verification. A receipt produced on a different host or with a mismatched recorded rustcVersion would still verify, because the host value is taken from the receipt itself.
findings.required_fix: Resolve the actual rustc host and version for the requested toolchain during --check (as scripts/check-package.py:102-105 already does) and require report['hostTarget'] and report['rustcVersion'] to match, or record explicitly in the receipt limitations that host identity is self-reported.

findings.description: The guard rejecting names starting with '.local/', 'contracts/', 'tools/' or 'node_modules/' is unreachable: line 44 has already restricted every accepted member to the explicit root_files set or 'src/'/'examples/' prefixes. Presenting an unreachable branch as a credential/development-input control is misleading when auditing the published-archive policy; only the suffix portion of the condition can still fire.
findings.required_fix: Either remove the unreachable prefix clause and keep the live suffix check, or reorder the two checks so the development/credential prefix guard is actually evaluated, and add a unit case that exercises whichever guard is retained.

findings.description: This new test file departs sharply from the formatting used by the surrounding tools/ suite (for example tools/test_management_package.py): multiple statements joined with semicolons on one line (lines 22, 29, 49, 54, 63), and call arguments written without spaces after commas (lines 39, 40, 44, 52, 59). Coverage is also missing the one resume hazard the implementation does not defend against: a later command in a resumed session replacing a receipt that an earlier checkpoint record is bound to.
findings.required_fix: Reformat to the repository's prevailing style (one statement per line, spaces after commas) and add a test asserting that mutating an earlier record's bound receipt during a resumed session is detected before the final report is written as passing.
